Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap on the ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2025 opener! Australia Women Under-19 has sent a strong statement, kicking off their campaign in style and setting the bar high for the rest of the tournament. Thanks for joining us for the live coverage! All you need to do is switch tabs and you'll have more thrilling cricket action, as the ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2025 continues. Until next time, cheers!

Caoimhe Bray is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH and she is up for a chat. Bray says the side played well and she is really happy to end up with three wickets. Mentions that she was excited to play this one and a performance as such from the team adds to it. Closes by saying that playing with the experienced players back at home has helped her a lot.

Lucy Hamilton, the skipper of Australia Women Under-19 says that they were clinical enough and they played a superb game of cricket. Says that it was great to see everyone perform to their abilities and start well. Closes by saying that it is great to have points on board at the start and the dressing room is totally excited for the next game.
Niamh Muir the skipper of Scotland Women Under-19 says that they lost a bit too many wickets early on and that cost them the game. Mentions that they will start the next game from scratch.
Stay tuned for the presentation ...

Earlier in the game, the Scotland Women's Under-19 team struggled to make an impact with the bat, managing only 48 runs in their opening innings. Only two Scottish batters reached double figures, leaving their team's batting lineup looking rather toothless. The Australian bowlers were on fire, with Eleanor Larosa and Caoimhe Bray claiming three wickets each, while Hasrat Gill took two. Tegan Williamson and Juliette Morton also chipped in with one wicket apiece.

The Scottish bowlers were unable to pose a challenge to the Australian batters, who wrapped up the match in a hurry. Nayma Sheikh was the only bowler who registered herself into the wickets column. This convincing win marks a strong start to Australia's campaign in the tournament.

Kate Pelle lit up the proceedings with an explosive first over, smashing three sixes to get Australia off to a flying start. Alongside her partner Ines McKeon, they made quick work of the modest Scottish total of 48. By the time Ines McKeon departed, Australia was almost at the finish line, and Kate Pelle, along with Lucy Hamilton, ensured they crossed it with ease. Although Australia secured a convincing win, a concern that emerged was Ines McKeon's vulnerability against leg-cutters and slower deliveries. Despite her short stay at the crease, she struggled against this type of delivery and was eventually dismissed by a leg-spinner. Knowing the metal of the Aussie, the team management will work on it.

A clinical and dominant display by the Australians, who made a strong statement in their opening match of the ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2025 by first bundling out Scotland to 48 and then chasing it down inside the first 7 with 9 wickets in hands.
That's a wrap to this game as Australia Women Under-19 wins this by 9 wickets. This was a full toss on off, Lucy Hamilton slaps this to long on for one.

UPDATE - Uh-oh! The weather has taken a turn for the worse, with the drizzle intensifying into a heavier downpour. The umpires have promptly asked the players to abandon the field, and we're now facing a potential delay. The crucial thing to note is that we're still 5 balls shy of 5 overs. A minimum of 5 overs must be bowled in the second innings for a match to be considered official and have a result. The Scots wouldn't mind not taking the field again but we are a long way off from that scenario.
